parsed.explanation: Division has no adult statewide bathroom or adult-care ban, documented, which prevents a 0.35-0.45 universal-exposure rating, but combined federal regime imposes birth-sex passport/facility rules, discrepancy-based entry refusal and possible fraud inquiry, and severe federal custody practices. Locally, no statewide nondiscrimination or hate-crime enhancement, with municipal protection only for ~46% of residents, leaves no recourse elsewhere. Youth exposures are board/district and not-yet-operative locally, aggravated nationally. This matches elevated, partially-remedied risk, not reduced risk with working nationwide remedies.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal policy since Feb 2025 processes new passports only M/F per birth sex; existing X passports valid to expiry. Discrepancy/reasonable doubt triggers refusal and extra evidence, suspected misrepresentation can support permanent fraud ineligibility; passports confiscated/blocked reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, limited waivers exist; ACLU suit and court challenges pending, several orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can escalate from entry processing to investigation, refusal, and potential fraud inquiry; state document rules do not override federal entry screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections from 2026 adopts conversion-therapy model: hair cutting, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans visitors/residents.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented operative remedy, monitoring, or placement-by-identity protocol for visitors; bureau stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers from 2025.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Arrest, immigration detention, or criminal charge (e.g. facilities trespass logic in other states) interfaces with birth-sex placement and hormone denial, turning a minor charge into severe custody exposure.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. Division: no statewide adult bathroom/changing-room ban, but one school district requires birth-sex or private alternative.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division retains adult facility access by identity by absence of statewide ban; 2022 district policy is district-only and does not extend to adult facilities.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities (airports, federal buildings) follow federal birth-sex rule even inside division; state protective absence does not cancel federal facilities exposure.

care_services.exposure: Federal corrections deny hormone medication; national orders target youth gender-affirming care and proposed rules would bar public insurance under 18. Division: no adult care ban.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned in division; August 2025 medical-board youth-care action is recommendation plus draft, not operative until law-department review and 30-day comment.
care_services.interaction: Travelling adult needing emergency care faces no documented division ward ban, but custody or federal facility placement can interrupt medication; minor care exposure is regulatory, not yet operative locally.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal framing treats trans identity as binary birth sex, removes gender-ideology materials, directs scrutiny of schools/teachers for social transition, and counterterrorism documents label 'radically pro-transgender' groups; passport cable creates suspicion-based refusal.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several executive orders blocked/enjoined and under litigation, limiting certainty of enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State-threat framing at federal level coexists with no documented division police targeting; prosecution efficiency does not mitigate documented federal custody/border practices.

minors_guardians.exposure: One school district binds trans students to birth-sex bathrooms or nurse/private alternative; state education board bars trans girls from female sports; federal order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition and youth-care restrictions.
minors_guardians.protection: Governor's broader student facility limit failed; youth-care draft not operative; visiting minor is not documented as subject to district school enrollment rules in dossier.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian/minor travelling together faces school/sports/care regulatory risk if enrolling or seeking care, plus federal orders create documentation and investigation exposure beyond division law.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No count of trans-specific violence in division and no general homicide baseline documented; division hate-crime statute does not list gender identity, so no state enhancement.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute punishes gender-identity bias; no documented division police pattern of targeting visitors.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of local violence data is not safety evidence; thin recourse outside municipalities plus federal custody severity means a police encounter carries disproportionate consequence.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide employment/housing/public-accommodations gender-identity protection; outside four municipalities (46% population) visitor has no state or municipal recourse in hotel/restaurant; enforcement of municipal ordinances not sourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Four municipalities prohibit gender-identity discrimination in employment, accommodations and housing; one ordinance survived 53-47 repeal vote; national courts have enjoined some orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Municipal protection does not reach federal entry, facilities, or custody, and does not cover majority of division; unknown enforcement weakens remedy weight.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than 0.45-A because division has no statewide adult bathroom ban and no documented trespass arrests there; federal facilities/passport rules are serious but narrower than all-public-buildings birth-sex ban.

Similar to 0.55-A: no trans-specific offence for adults, recurring federal border/facility friction, incomplete remedies, and slow or geographically patchy recourse, with custody undocumented there but documented-severe here.

Lower than 0.65-A because border does not accept X for new issues and can refuse on discrepancy, federal facilities are birth-sex restricted, and division lacks statewide nondiscrimination recourse outside municipalities.

Higher than 0.35-D because no current survey documents large-majority visitor-facing discrimination in hotels/transport in division, and no unremedied statewide universal facility exclusion for adults is documented.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: division offers adult facility and adult care access, but federal birth-sex document, facility, and custody rules govern key journey stages and cannot be cancelled by local tolerance. Municipal protections cover less than half the population; elsewhere no recourse. Youth rules are mostly board/district or non-operative drafts locally, with harsher federal orders partly enjoined. Result is elevated risk driven by federal interactions and thin remedies, mitigated by absence of local adult bans and absence of documented local targeting.
